angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 740,921 km at 155.01 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4511 +/- 0.0132 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 155.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.065 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Ulmer-Moll et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2449 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.258U/abstract): 740,921 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.079 +/- 0.045 solar masses from Ulmer-Moll et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2449 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.258U/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6021 +/- 62 K from Ulmer-Moll et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2449 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.258U/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ulmer-Moll et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2449 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.258U/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2449.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.416, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
